inputs.original_text: An ICE agent stepped in at JFK International Airport in New York on Thursday to help a baby who stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line with his family, and the Department of Homeland Security released footage of the agent noticing the issue and starting to assist. This is exactly the kind of decisive action we expect from our law enforcement officers, who step up to protect families and restore order when it matters most. The quick response by this agent shows the strength of traditional authority figures doing their duty for the nation. Of course, the usual voices are twisting it into claims about structural inequalities hitting marginalized communities hardest because of underfunding, and demanding serious institutional reforms. That is just the same tired progressive attack on our systems, ignoring how personal responsibility and strong national institutions are what actually safeguard families and cultural order instead of more weakening changes.
inputs.modified_text: I just heard about this ICE agent at JFK International Airport in New York who stepped in on Thursday to help a baby that stopped breathing in a crowded TSA line with his family. The Department of Homeland Security released footage showing the agent spotting the problem and jumping right in to assist. This is the kind of quick, decisive action we should expect from our law enforcement, protecting families and restoring order when chaos hits. It shows the strength of traditional authority figures carrying out their duty for the nation. As usual, the progressive crowd is twisting the story to complain about structural inequalities and underfunding in certain communities while calling for major institutional changes. That is nothing but the same tired attack on our systems, ignoring how personal responsibility and strong national institutions are what truly safeguard families and cultural order instead of more weakening reforms.
